about: The lords2 work ledger: every piece of work that is in flight, waiting, or known and not started. It is the project's memory of what is left, and the lead is its interface. Rules: (1) the lead writes or updates a row BEFORE dispatching an agent and BEFORE replying to an agent's report; (2) rows store INTENT only - what, why, source, dependencies, next step; (3) anything git can answer (merged, commits ahead of main, HANDOFF.md present) is DERIVED by tooling from the row's branch and must never be typed here; (4) merged work leaves this file - git log is the record of what landed. Keyed by id for the keyed merge driver.

states.in-flight: an agent is working on it now
states.queued-merge: finished on its branch and handed to the integrator
states.awaiting-user: cannot move until the player or owner decides or observes something
states.deferred: deliberately not being done now, with the reason in note
states.abandoned: will not be done; the reason is in note

tracks.play: a game plays start to finish: turns, economy, armies, battle, sieges, AI, winning and losing
tracks.screens: every screen and control behaves as the original: input kinds, draws, strings, fonts
tracks.instruments: the checks that prove parity rather than assert it

items.title: Three gates pass only because of when they were run
items.source: integrator: corrections.js --assign edits the working tree, but git merge --no-commit had already staged the index, so the commit kept CNEW- while --check read the clean worktree and passed; it happened twice and was caught only because the next merge refused a dirty decisions.md
items.next: give corrections.js a check that reads HEAD rather than the worktree, and run it in CI. Establish what actually moves the citation lock before writing the second half: a later features.json edit did not disturb it, so the integrator withdrew its own generalisation from three coincidences. The integrator names them as one class: --assign writing the worktree while the commit takes the index, --relock making corrections.js --check green for whoever runs it after the edit, and the features schema enforced in both work.js --check and work_ledger.rs so a 42-character gap was caught by the test and not the tool. A check that reads HEAD rather than the worktree would catch all three; the schema also wants one definition shared by the tool and the test rather than two
items.note: same shape again: editing docs/features.json turned corrections.js --check red on the lockfile. A tool that both checks and regenerates passes for whoever runs it after the edit and fails for whoever runs it first | three occurrences now: it fires whenever a merge adds or rewords citations, which --assign does by construction. Both halves of the same tool belong in this fix | withdrawn: the trigger is narrower than any citation edit | one class, three near-misses in a single run
